editorial:
Imagine being the only person in the room who refuses to change your ideas just to fit in. You will meet Howard Roark, a bold architect who would rather work in a granite quarry than design buildings that look like every other boring block in the city. He is stubborn and doesn't care what people think of him, which makes him both fascinating and frustrating. Along the way, he meets Dominique, a woman who is just as tough and mysterious as he is. The whole movie feels like a battle between one man's vision and a world that wants him to play by the rules.

The acting is strong, especially how the lead actors show a lot of tension without saying much. While the dialogue can feel a bit like a long lecture sometimes, the drama keeps you interested. If you like stories about rebels and strong personalities, you will love this. It is a great pick for a quiet weekend night when you want something a bit more serious.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head in a big courtroom scene where Roark defends his work. He explains that he creates for himself, not for others. The big twist happens when he reveals he designed the Cortlandt Homes project, but the owners changed his plans without telling him. Since they ruined his design, he blows the building up with dynamite. Instead of going to jail, the jury lets him go because they agree with his point about artistic truth.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about independence and fighting the system.
